content.text:
Fixed. `s = "caf\u00e9"` now parses to `{'s': 'café'}`.

`parse_hex_char` in `src/tomli/_parser.py` advanced the position by `hex_len - 1` instead of `hex_len`. That made the string parser read the last hex digit a second time, so the `9` was appended after `é`. This affected the `\x`, `\u` and `\U` escapes.

I added a regression test, `test_unicode_escape_consumes_exact_digits`, in `tests/test_misc.py`. It covers all three escape forms, including cases where a literal digit or character follows the escape. The full suite passes (19 tests, 1 skipped).

The position passed to the "not a Unicode scalar value" error is now one character later than before. No existing test depended on it.
